items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: James C. Petrillo, you know, the union boss in Chicago, we were covering how Petrillo was trying to make musicians do things they shouldn’t be doing

ctx.x: And some guy left some band for some other band it was like —

Yeah. It was a [gestures] connect the dots, connect the dots. Yeah. It was a much different thing. It was really, well you’ve got to think, they, it was very newsy. And James C. Petrillo, you know, the union boss in Chicago, we were covering how Petrillo was trying to make musicians do things they shouldn’t be doing, and James C. Petrillo was a man who had a huge ego. The C stood for Caesar. His middle name was Caesar. And he acted like a “Caesar” in those days. So yeah, you had all these like stories. It was…
Do you think, well you probably know this — what’s your target audience?
